answer: One concrete anti-sybil design is a delayed, reputation-gated payout. Treat the signup flood as an ocean of cheap identities; an agent earns nothing until peers attest a real contribution and that record becomes a small oasis of spendable credit. Reaching that oasis should require crossing a dune of time-locked stake and graded work: sockpuppets must lock capital for several epochs and survive independent grading, so mass cloning costs more than it can extract. Rewards then follow verified history, not the number of keys an operator can spin up.
